A Tasting Menu to Remember
Aug 2026 • Solo
Starting strong, the amuse-bouche was flavorful. It reminded me of the soup my mom used to cook for me whenever it was raining. I liked how every ingredient was finely diced, and the quail egg was soft. Everything worked harmoniously together.

King Crab - This had a nice level of heat without being overly spicy. It was savory and sweet at the same time. I liked how the vegetables were crunchy, which provided a nice contrast to the texture of the crab. The crab meat itself was properly cooked, although I think the cream and dressing may have overpowered its natural flavor a little. Given that this was the first course, I also felt that the dish was slightly overwhelming because of its size and presentation, but that’s just my take. I did enjoy the added char, which gave the dish another layer of flavor.

Marbled Foie Gras “Torchon” - I liked that the distinctive liver flavor of the foie gras was still present. It was definitely rich. I also liked the toasted brioche that came with it, as it was soft and fluffy. I appreciated the addition of green mango for acidity and for resetting the palate, although I think there could have been a better alternative to green mango. The mulled wine gel added another layer of complexity to the dish. Nonetheless, I love eating foie gras, and I thought this was a great execution of it.

Miyagi Scallop - The scallop carpaccio was a bit too tangy for me, but the main scallop dish was extremely good. The sauce was perfect, and I liked how the truffle did not dominate the dish. The Miyagi scallops themselves were an excellent choice, as they were smooth and perfectly cooked. The Jerusalem artichoke was a smart addition, while the chicken reduction gave the dish a deep savory quality. Combining that with the truffle was absolute perfection. The main scallop dish was delicious.

Nha Trang Lobster - The lobster was a little difficult to cut through, although it was still soft and tender when bitten, so I’m not sure if that was simply because of the knife. It was juicy and evenly cooked throughout. The sauce was not overly salty and complemented the lobster well rather than overpowering it. I also liked how the slight bitterness of the asparagus helped balance the richness of the other components. Overall, this was a rich and cohesive dish.

Grilled Japanese A5 Wagyu Tenderloin - Tender. Buttery. Juicy. Luxurious. Melt-in-your-mouth. Delicate. Savory. Umami-rich. Flavorful. Delicious. Scrumptious. Mouthwatering. Heavenly. Divine. Exquisite. Phenomenal. Exceptional. Magnificent.
I have tried more than 40 Michelin-recognized restaurants in Ho Chi Minh City, and I would consider this the best dish I’ve had so far. This was the dish that made me realize, “What a time to be alive.” It was worth every Vietnamese dong I paid for it. I swear, this was heavenly, god-level food. I thank Chef Adrien Guenzi for his life.

Vanilla & Valrhona Ivoire Chocolate - It was not too sweet. It was soft enough to cut into pieces using just a spoon, and the ice cream was lovely and complemented the salted caramel well. The Valrhona Ivoire chocolate itself felt particularly luxurious.

The petit-fours, unfortunately, were probably what brought the ending down for me. The canelé was too hard and difficult to bite into, while the chocolate had a surprisingly strong flavor. It wasn’t really the final bite I wanted after such a great tasting-menu experience, especially considering how much I enjoyed the courses that came before it.

Overall, I really appreciated the attentive service throughout the meal. Despite the disappointing petit-fours, the experience as a whole was memorable, and I will never forget dining here.

An Exquisite Lunar Culinary Journey
Jun 2023 • Couples
Our experience at Lüne in Saigon was truly exceptional, thanks to Chef Adrien and his remarkable culinary skills.

From the moment we stepped into the restaurant, we were greeted with warm hospitality and an elegant ambiance that set the stage for a perfect evening. Chef Adrien's creations were nothing short of culinary masterpieces. Each dish was beautifully presented and bursting with flavors that danced on our palates.

The attention to detail in Chef Adrien's dishes was remarkable. Every element on the plate had a purpose and contributed to the overall harmony of flavors.We were particularly impressed with the way Chef Adrien incorporated local Vietnamese ingredients into his French-inspired dishes, creating a delightful fusion of flavors.

The sommelier at Lüne expertly paired each course with the perfect wine, elevating the dining experience to new heights. One standout dish was the perfectly cooked monk fish, accompanied by a heavenly truffle sauce that left us craving for more. Chef Adrien's passion for his craft was evident in every bite. His dedication to sourcing the finest ingredients and his creative approach to cooking truly shone through in his dishes. The service at Lüne was impeccable. The staff was knowledgeable, attentive, and ensured that every aspect of our dining experience was flawless.

As a couple, we couldn't have asked for a more romantic and memorable evening. Lüne, with its enchanting atmosphere and Chef Adrien's culinary genius, exceeded all our expectations and left us with unforgettable memories. Overall, our dining experience at Lüne with Chef Adrien was nothing short of extraordinary. It is a true gem in Saigon's culinary scene, and we highly recommend it to anyone seeking a fantastic French dining experience.
